statement:
Use the binomial expansion to show that the coefficient of $x^r$ in the expansion of $(1-x)^{-3}$ is $\tfrac12(r+1)(r+2)$.

(i) Show that the coefficient of $x^r$ in the expansion of
$$\frac{1-x+2x^2}{(1-x)^3}$$
is $r^2+1$, and hence find the sum of the series
$$1+\frac22+\frac54+\frac{10}{8}+\frac{17}{16}+\frac{26}{32}+\frac{37}{64}+\frac{50}{128}+\cdots.$$

(ii) Find the sum of the series
$$1+2+\frac94+2+\frac{25}{16}+\frac98+\frac{49}{64}+\cdots.$$
solution:
By the binomial theorem for negative exponents,
$$(1-x)^{-3}=\sum_{r=0}^{\infty}\binom{r+2}{2}x^r=\sum_{r=0}^{\infty}\frac{(r+1)(r+2)}{2}x^r.$$

(i) The coefficient of $x^r$ in $\dfrac{1-x+2x^2}{(1-x)^3}$ is
$$\frac{(r+1)(r+2)}{2}-\frac{r(r+1)}{2}+2\cdot\frac{(r-1)r}{2}=\frac{(r+1)[(r+2)-r]}{2}+r(r-1)=(r+1)+r^2-r=r^2+1.$$

So $\dfrac{1-x+2x^2}{(1-x)^3}=\sum_{r=0}^{\infty}(r^2+1)x^r$. Substituting $x=\tfrac12$:
$$1+\frac22+\frac54+\frac{10}{8}+\cdots=\sum_{r=0}^{\infty}(r^2+1)\left(\frac12\right)^r=\frac{1-\tfrac12+2(\tfrac12)^2}{(1-\tfrac12)^3}=\frac{1-\tfrac12+\tfrac12}{\tfrac18}=8.$$

(ii) The terms $1,\frac22,\frac94,\frac{16}{8},\frac{25}{16},\frac{36}{32},\frac{49}{64},\dots$ are $\dfrac{n^2}{2^{n-1}}$ for $n=1,2,3,\dots$. So the sum is
$$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{n^2}{2^{n-1}}=2\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{n^2}{2^n}.$$

Using the standard result $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}n^2x^n=\dfrac{x(1+x)}{(1-x)^3}$ (from differentiating $\sum nx^n$), with $x=\tfrac12$:
$$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{n^2}{2^n}=\frac{\tfrac12(1+\tfrac12)}{(1-\tfrac12)^3}=\frac{\tfrac34}{\tfrac18}=6.$$
Hence the sum is $2\times6=12$.
